section_1.title: The Core Intuition: Rates of Change
section_1.content: Briefly review the derivative as a 'rate of change' (slope). Introduce the concept of a functional relationship where the rate of change of a quantity depends on the quantity itself, rather than just time.
section_1.example: Visualize a 'rabbit population' graph where the number of rabbits determines how fast the population grows.

section_2.title: Defining the ODE
section_2.content: Define an Ordinary Differential Equation as an equation involving a function and its derivatives. Differentiate between an algebraic equation (finding a number) and an ODE (finding a function).
section_2.example: Show the equation dy/dt = ky. Explain that the solution isn't a single point, but a curve that 'follows the slope' defined by the equation.

section_3.title: Visualizing Solutions: Slope Fields
section_3.content: Introduce Slope Fields (Direction Fields). Explain how a grid of arrows representing the derivative at each point acts as a 'compass' to map out potential solution curves.
section_3.example: An animation showing a drop of ink in a flowing stream; the ink trace follows the vector field, illustrating how the differential equation dictates the path of the 'particle'.

section_4.title: The Role of Initial Conditions
section_4.content: Explain that an ODE describes a 'family' of curves. Introduce the Initial Value Problem (IVP), where a starting state 'pins down' a specific unique solution curve.
section_4.example: A catapult simulation: The ODE defines the trajectory path, while the 'Initial Condition' (angle and force of launch) determines exactly where the projectile lands.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-World Bridge
section_5.content: Conclude with the power of ODEs in modeling reality (physics, biology, economics). Emphasize that solving an ODE is finding the underlying 'rule' that guides a dynamic system.
section_5.example: Briefly mention how an ODE describes the cooling of a hot cup of coffee, linking back to the initial concept of 'rate of change'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side starts at x=3
                x = 3.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
